require "rails_helper"

describe Admin::Legislation::ProposalsController, :admin do
  describe "PATCH select" do
    let(:proposal) { create(:legislation_proposal) }

    it "selects the proposal" do
      expect do
        patch :select, xhr: true, params: { id: proposal.id, process_id: proposal.process.id }
      end.to change { proposal.reload.selected? }.from(false).to(true)

      expect(response).to be_successful
    end

    it "does not modify already selected proposals" do
      proposal.update!(selected: true)

      expect do
        patch :select, xhr: true, params: { id: proposal.id, process_id: proposal.process.id }
      end.not_to change { proposal.reload.selected? }
    end

    it "redirects admins without JavaScript to the same page" do
      request.env["HTTP_REFERER"] = admin_proposals_path

      patch :select, params: { id: proposal.id, process_id: proposal.process.id }

      expect(response).to redirect_to admin_proposals_path
      expect(flash[:notice]).to eq "Proposal updated successfully."
    end
  end

  describe "PATCH deselect" do
    let(:proposal) { create(:legislation_proposal, :selected) }

    it "deselects the proposal" do
      expect do
        patch :deselect, xhr: true, params: { id: proposal.id, process_id: proposal.process.id }
      end.to change { proposal.reload.selected? }.from(true).to(false)

      expect(response).to be_successful
    end

    it "does not modify non-selected proposals" do
      proposal.update!(selected: false)

      expect do
        patch :deselect, xhr: true, params: { id: proposal.id, process_id: proposal.process.id }
      end.not_to change { proposal.reload.selected? }
    end

    it "redirects admins without JavaScript to the same page" do
      request.env["HTTP_REFERER"] = admin_proposals_path

      patch :deselect, params: { id: proposal.id, process_id: proposal.process.id }

      expect(response).to redirect_to admin_proposals_path
      expect(flash[:notice]).to eq "Proposal updated successfully."
    end
  end
end

# This module is expanded in order to make it easier to use polymorphic
# routes with nested resources in the admin namespace
module ActionDispatch::Routing::UrlFor
  def resource_hierarchy_for(resource)
    resolve = resolve_for(resource)

    if resolve
      if resolve.last.is_a?(Hash)
        [resolve.first, *resolve.last.values]
      else
        resolve
      end
    else
      resource
    end
  end

  def admin_polymorphic_path(resource, options = {})
    namespaced_polymorphic_path(:admin, resource, options)
  end

  def sdg_management_polymorphic_path(resource, options = {})
    namespaced_polymorphic_path(:sdg_management, resource, options)
  end

  def management_polymorphic_path(resource, options = {})
    if resource.class.name == "Budget::Investment"
      management_budget_investment_path(resource.budget, resource, options)
    else
      namespaced_polymorphic_path("management", resource, options)
    end
  end

  def namespaced_polymorphic_path(namespace, resource, options = {})
    if %w[Budget::Group Budget::Heading Legislation::DraftVersion Legislation::Proposal Legislation::Question
          Poll::Booth Poll::BoothAssignment Poll::Officer Poll::Question Poll::Question::Option
          Poll::Question::Option::Video Poll::Shift SDG::LocalTarget].include?(resource.class.name)
      resolve = resolve_for(resource)
      resolve_options = resolve.pop

      polymorphic_path([namespace.to_sym, *resolve], options.merge(resolve_options))
    else
      polymorphic_path([namespace.to_sym, *resource_hierarchy_for(resource)], options)
    end
  end

  private

    def resolve_for(resource)
      polymorphic_mapping(resource)&.send(:eval_block, self, resource, {})
    end
end

      get "/graphql", params: { query: query_string }

      expect(response.parsed_body["data"]["proposal"]["title"]).to eq(proposal.title)

      expect(response.parsed_body["data"]).to be nil
      expect(response.parsed_body["errors"]).to be_present
    end

    specify "without query string" do
      get "/graphql"

      expect(response).to have_http_status(:bad_request)
      expect(response.parsed_body["message"]).to eq("Query string not present")
    end
  end

  describe "handles POST request" do
    let(:json_headers) { { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/json" } }

    specify "with json-encoded query string inside body" do
      post "/graphql", params: { query: query_string }.to_json,

      expect(response.parsed_body["data"]["proposal"]["title"]).to eq(proposal.title)
    end

    specify "with raw query string inside body" do
      graphql_headers = { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/graphql" }

      expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
      expect(response.parsed_body["data"]["proposal"]["title"]).to eq(proposal.title)
    end

    specify "with malformed query string" do
      post "/graphql", params: { query: "Malformed query string" }.to_json, headers: json_headers

      expect(response.parsed_body["data"]).to be nil
      expect(response.parsed_body["errors"]).to be_present
    end

    it "without query string" do
      post "/graphql", headers: json_headers

      expect(response).to have_http_status(:bad_request)
      expect(response.parsed_body["message"]).to eq("Query string not present")
    end
  end

  describe "correctly parses query variables" do
    specify "when absent" do
      get "/graphql", params: { query: query_string }

      expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    end

    specify "when specified as the 'null' string" do

      expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)

      expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)

      post "/graphql", params: { query: query_string }

      expect(response).to have_http_status(:forbidden)
    end

describe Mailer do
  describe "#comment" do
    before do
      allow_any_instance_of(ActionMailer::MessageDelivery).to receive(:deliver_later), &:deliver_now
    end

    it "sends emails in the user's locale" do
      user = create(:user, locale: "es")
      proposal = create(:proposal, author: user)
      comment = create(:comment, commentable: proposal)

      email = I18n.with_locale :en do
        Mailer.comment(comment)
      end

      expect(email.subject).to include("comentado")
    end

    it "reads the from address at runtime" do
      Setting["mailer_from_name"] = "New organization"
      Setting["mailer_from_address"] = "new@consul.dev"

      email = Mailer.comment(create(:comment))

      expect(email).to deliver_from "New organization <new@consul.dev>"
    end

    it "sends emails for comments on legislation proposals" do
      email = Mailer.comment(create(:legislation_proposal_comment))

      expect(email.subject).to include("commented on your proposal")
    end

    context "Proposal comments" do
      let(:user)     { create(:user, email_on_comment: true) }
      let(:proposal) { create(:proposal, author: user) }

      it "Send email on proposal comment" do
        comment_on(proposal)

        email = open_last_email
        expect(email).to have_subject "Someone has commented on your citizen proposal"
        expect(email).to deliver_to(proposal.author)
        expect(email).to have_body_text proposal_path(proposal)
        expect(email).to have_body_text "To unsubscribe from these emails, visit"
        expect(email).to have_body_text edit_subscriptions_path(token: proposal.author.subscriptions_token)
        expect(email).to have_body_text 'and uncheck "Notify me by email when someone ' \
                                        'comments on my contents"'
      end

      it "Do not send email about own proposal comments" do
        comment_on(proposal, user)
        expect { open_last_email }.to raise_error "No email has been sent!"
      end

      it "Do not send email about proposal comment unless set in preferences" do
        user.update!(email_on_comment: false)
        comment_on(proposal)
        expect { open_last_email }.to raise_error "No email has been sent!"
      end
    end

    context "Debate comments" do
      let(:user)   { create(:user, email_on_comment: true) }
      let(:debate) { create(:debate, author: user) }

      scenario "Send email on debate comment" do
        comment_on(debate)

        email = open_last_email
        expect(email).to have_subject "Someone has commented on your debate"

require "rails_helper"

  end

    describe "Should detect remote_translations" do
      it "When collections are not defined in current locale" do
        debates = create_list(:debate, 3)
        other_debates = create_list(:debate, 3)

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(debates, other_debates).count).to eq 6
        end
      end

      it "When we have nil as argument and collections are not defined in current locale" do
        debates = create_list(:debate, 3)

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(debates, nil).count).to eq 3
        end
      end

      it "When we have [] as argument and collections are not defined in current locale" do
        debates = create_list(:debate, 3)

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(debates, []).count).to eq 3
        end
      end

      it "When widget feeds are not defined in current locale" do
        create_list(:debate, 3)
        create_list(:legislation_process, 3)
        create(:widget_feed, kind: "debates")
        create(:widget_feed, kind: "processes")
        widget_feeds = Widget::Feed.active

        I18n.with_locale(:es) do
          expect(detect_remote_translations(widget_feeds).count).to eq 6
        end
      end
    end

    it "When remote translations are not configured should not detect remote_translations" do
      allow(RemoteTranslations::Caller).to receive(:configured?).and_return(false)
      debate = create(:debate)
      comment = create(:comment, commentable: debate)

      I18n.with_locale(:es) do
        expect(detect_remote_translations([debate, comment])).to eq []
      end
    end

    it "When defined in current locale should not detect remote_translations" do
      debate = create(:debate)
      comment = create(:comment, commentable: debate)

      expect(detect_remote_translations([debate, comment])).to eq []
    end

    it "When resource class is not translatable should not detect remote_translations" do
      legislation_proposal = create(:legislation_proposal)

      I18n.with_locale(:es) do
        expect(detect_remote_translations([legislation_proposal])).to eq []
      end
    end
  end
end

require "rails_helper"

describe ActsAsTaggableOn do
  describe "Tagging" do
    describe "when tagging debates or investments" do
      let(:investment) { create(:budget_investment) }
      let(:debate) { create(:debate) }

      it "increases and decreases the tag's custom counters" do
        tag = Tag.create!(name: "foo")

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.budget_investments_count).to eq(0)

        investment.tag_list.add("foo")
        investment.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.budget_investments_count).to eq(1)

        debate.tag_list.add("foo")
        debate.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(1)
        expect(tag.budget_investments_count).to eq(1)

        investment.tag_list.remove("foo")
        investment.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(1)
        expect(tag.budget_investments_count).to eq(0)

        debate.tag_list.remove("foo")
        debate.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.budget_investments_count).to eq(0)
      end
    end
  end

    stub_const("#{Activity}::VALID_ACTIONS", %w[custom])

    it "creates an activity entry" do

      expect(Activity.on(proposal)).to match_array [activity1, activity2, activity3]

  end

      activity5 = create(:activity, user: user1, action: "block", actionable: create(:user))

      )
    end
  end

      expect(Activity.on_users).to eq [on_user]

  end

describe Image do
  let(:image) { create(:image, attachment: fixture_file_upload("clippy.jpg")) }

  it_behaves_like "image validations", "budget_investment_image"
  it_behaves_like "image validations", "budget_image"

  end

  describe "#variant" do
    it "processes variants with combine_options from old Active Storage URLs" do
      old_transformations = {
        combine_options: { gravity: "center", resize: "300x300^", crop: "300x300+0+0" }
      }

      expect { image.attachment.variant(old_transformations).processed }.not_to raise_error
    end

    it "preserves Rails validations for normal transformations" do
      unsafe_transformations = { system: "dangerous_command" }

      expect { image.attachment.variant(unsafe_transformations).processed }.to raise_error(
        ActiveStorage::Transformers::ImageProcessingTransformer::UnsupportedImageProcessingMethod
      )
    end

    it "validates operations unwrapped from combine_options" do
      legacy_with_unsafe = {
        combine_options: { system: "dangerous_command" }
      }

      expect { image.attachment.variant(legacy_with_unsafe).processed }.to raise_error(
        ActiveStorage::Transformers::ImageProcessingTransformer::UnsupportedImageProcessingMethod
      )
    end
  end

  end

  describe "#variant" do
    it "processes variants with combine_options from old Active Storage URLs" do
      old_transformations = {
        combine_options: { gravity: "center", resize: "300x300^", crop: "300x300+0+0" }
      }

      expect { image.attachment.variant(old_transformations).processed }.not_to raise_error
    end

    it "preserves Rails validations for normal transformations" do
      unsafe_transformations = { system: "dangerous_command" }

      )
    end

      legacy_with_unsafe = {
        combine_options: { system: "dangerous_command" }
      }

      expect { image.attachment.variant(legacy_with_unsafe).processed }.to raise_error(
        ActiveStorage::Transformers::ImageProcessingTransformer::UnsupportedImageProcessingMethod
      )
    end

require "rails_helper"

describe SDG::ProcessEnabled do
  describe "#enabled?" do
    context "SDG feature and namespace are enabled" do
      before do
        Setting["feature.sdg"] = true
        %w[debates proposals polls budgets legislation].each do |process_name|
          Setting["sdg.process.#{process_name}"] = true
        end
      end

      it "returns true with relatable records" do
        SDG::Related::RELATABLE_TYPES.each do |relatable_type|
          process = SDG::ProcessEnabled.new(relatable_type.constantize.new)

          expect(process).to be_enabled
        end
      end

      it "returns true with relatable class names" do
        SDG::Related::RELATABLE_TYPES.each do |relatable_type|
          process = SDG::ProcessEnabled.new(relatable_type)

          expect(process).to be_enabled
        end
      end

      it "returns true with relatable controller paths" do
        process = SDG::ProcessEnabled.new("budgets/investments")

        expect(process).to be_enabled
      end

      it "returns false when record or name are not a relatable type" do
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new(build(:legislation_question))).not_to be_enabled
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new("Legislation::Question")).not_to be_enabled
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new("officing/booth")).not_to be_enabled
      end
    end

    context "SDG feature is disabled" do
      before do
        Setting["feature.sdg"] = false
        Setting["sdg.process.debates"] = true
      end

      it "returns false" do
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new(build(:debate))).not_to be_enabled
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new("Debate")).not_to be_enabled
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new("debates")).not_to be_enabled
      end
    end

    context "Some SDG processes are disabled" do
      before do
        Setting["feature.sdg"] = true
        Setting["sdg.process.debates"] = true
        Setting["sdg.process.proposals"] = false
      end

      it "returns false for disabled processes" do
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new(build(:proposal))).not_to be_enabled
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new("Proposal")).not_to be_enabled
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new("proposals")).not_to be_enabled
      end

      it "returns true for enabled processes" do
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new(build(:debate))).to be_enabled
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new("Debate")).to be_enabled
        expect(SDG::ProcessEnabled.new("debates")).to be_enabled
      end
    end
  end
end

    end

  end
end

**SDG Review Analysis: An Unexpected Revelation**

Okay, so I'm diving into this `SDG::Review` model, and something's *really* jumping out at me. Firstly, it's crystal clear that `SDG::Review` is exclusively accessed through `has_one :sdg_review, as: :relatable` relationships on those kept models – `Debate`, `Budget::Investment`, `Poll`, `Legislation::Process`, and `Legislation::Proposal`. The entire application *never* queries `SDG::Review.all` or uses that `sdg_review.relatable` method directly! This means the need for a `default_scope` is completely unnecessary here! That's a huge simplification, right off the bat.

Then, there's the `where.missing(:sdg_review)` issue. I think I've figured it out. ActiveRecord's `where.missing` method, it turns out, *only* rewrites table aliases when dealing with hash-based predicates within `PredicateBuilder`. Things like `where(relatable_type: ...)` or `where.not(relatable_type: "Proposal").or(where(relatable_type: nil))`. But *not* when using manual `arel_table` nodes. That's because the `arel_table` is bound to the original `Table.new("sdg_reviews")` before any aliasing happens. Whereas a simple `where(col: ...)` goes through the `PredicateBuilder`, so the alias gets applied.

Wait a sec... Hold on. Let me look at this `where.not(col: "Proposal").or(where(col: nil))` scenario. Does *that* code actually set any attributes on `.new`? Nope! Not even. Neither `where.not(...)` nor `.or(...)` sets any attributes on `.new`. ActiveRecord *only* sets attributes from positive equality predicates, like `where(col: scalar)`. And since `where.not(col: "Proposal").or(where(col: nil))` goes through `PredicateBuilder`, ActiveRecord *automatically* rewrites those table aliases in `where.missing`, `left_joins`, self-joins – everything!

Okay, time to double-check this in `rails runner` and then run the model specs. Just to be completely sure. This could simplify things considerably.

messages.content: Let's print all 375 unused i18n keys and inspect citizen-proposal entries in `config/locales/en/activerecord.yml`.
messages.thinking:
**My Immediate Assessment and Proposed Action Plan**

Okay, first things first - fantastic! The initial check shows *no* missing translations. That's a great starting point. Now, I see `i18n-tasks` offers the `remove-unused` command, which is a powerful tool. However, with 375 keys potentially on the chopping block, I can't just blindly run it. We need to be absolutely certain of what we're removing.

My immediate next step is to get a complete list of those 375 unused key names. I want a clear view of every single one. Then, I need to thoroughly inspect them, *especially* against their expected locations. I want to confirm they're all related to the modules: citizen proposals, dashboard, notifications, and links. It's a critical step.

Furthermore, I have to give *special attention* to `config/locales/en/activerecord.yml`. I recall that `i18n-tasks.yml` specifies `activerecord.*` is in `ignore_unused`. So, while the tool might not flag those, we'll need to manually clean up anything related to `proposal`, `proposal_notification`, `dashboard/*`, `email_digest`, and `recommended_proposals` from that file. This is crucial for maintaining a clean and accurate translation system. Also, I'll need to verify `"See proposals"` in `verification.yml`, the `"Proposals"` shortcut in `pages.yml` and `welcome.recommended.help` in `general.yml`..

So, let's get those key names listed and then carefully cross-reference them with the specific locale files to eliminate any false positives. Only then will I feel comfortable running that `remove-unused` command with the `-y` flag. That's the prudent approach here, ensuring data integrity before any deletion.

arguments.command:
cd /app && bundle exec rails runner '
  require "i18n/tasks"
  i18n = I18n::Tasks::BaseTask.new
  i18n.unused_keys.leaves.each { |k| puts k.full_key }
' && echo "=== activerecord.yml ===" && cat config/locales/en/activerecord.yml

messages.content: Let's run `bundle exec i18n-tasks remove-unused -y` and inspect the remaining citizen-proposal keys inside `ignore_unused` namespaces in `config/locales/en/`.
messages.thinking:
**My Immediate Task: Purging Unused I18n Keys**

Okay, so looking at this list, every single one of those 375 unused i18n keys is directly tied to the citizen proposal system – proposals, notifications, the dashboard, and relevant links. The implication is crystal clear: we need to clean up the i18n files, which is a perfect opportunity to declutter. My initial move? Run `bundle exec i18n-tasks remove-unused -y` immediately to eliminate the obvious dead code and unnecessary keys. This should remove the unused keys.

However, I'm not stopping there. I also need to meticulously inspect the `config/locales/en/activerecord.yml`, `activemodel.yml`, `general.yml`, `verification.yml`, `pages.yml`, `moderation.yml`, and `admin.yml` files. I have to scan for any `ignore_unused`-masked citizen-proposal keys. Examples are keys like `activerecord.models.proposal`, `activerecord.models.proposal_notification`, `activerecord.models.dashboard/*`, `activerecord.attributes.proposal_notification`, `activerecord.attributes.dashboard/*`, `activerecord.attributes.link`, `activerecord.attributes.user.{email_digest,recommended_proposals}`, `activerecord.errors.models.{proposal,proposal_notification}`, `notifications.notification.action.proposal_notification`, `related_content.content_title.proposal`, `admin.shared.search.label.proposals`, `sdg_management.menu.proposals`, `moderation.proposals.index.orders.confidence_score`, `users.show.filters.proposals`, etc. These files might contain keys that are intentionally "ignored" by the linter, but still relevant to the citizen proposal system. We can't just blindly remove them.

The crucial first step is executing `bundle exec i18n-tasks remove-unused -y` right now. After that, I'll systematically comb through the specified YAML files to ensure we haven't inadvertently deleted anything critical while removing the unused keys.

arguments.command: cd /app && bundle exec i18n-tasks remove-unused -y && grep -rn -i "proposal\|dashboard\|email_digest" config/locales/en/

Ensuring healthy lives and promoting well-being at all ages is essential to sustainable development. Currently, the world is facing a global health crisis unlike any other — COVID-19 is spreading human suffering, destabilizing the global economy and upending the lives of billions of people around the globe. 

Before the pandemic, major progress was made in improving the health of millions of people. Significant strides were made in increasing life expectancy and reducing some of the common killers associated with child and maternal mortality. But more efforts are needed to fully eradicate a wide range of diseases and address many different persistent and emerging health issues. By focusing on providing more efficient funding of health systems, improved sanitation and hygiene, and increased access to physicians, significant progress can be made in helping to save the lives of millions.

Health emergencies such as COVID-19 pose a global risk and have shown the critical need for preparedness. The United Nations Development Programme highlighted huge disparities in countries’ abilities to cope with and recover from the COVID-19 crisis. The pandemic provides a watershed moment for health emergency preparedness and for investment in critical 21st century public services. 

config/locales/en/sdg.yml:557: long_description:

Nevertheless, more focused attention is needed to improve access to clean and safe cooking fuels and technologies for 3 billion people, to expand the use of renewable energy beyond the electricity sector, and to increase electrification in sub-Saharan Africa.

The Energy Progress Report provides global dashboard to register progress on energy access, energy efficiency and renewable energy. It assesses the progress made by each country on these three pillars and provides a snapshot of how far we are from achieving the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals targets.

**Smoke Test Execution Plan: A Deep Dive**

Okay, so the i18n specs are looking good – 7 examples and no failures. Fantastic!  Before we proceed, I'll quickly remove those three lines in `config/locales/en/activerecord.yml`.  Done.

Now, we're at a critical stage. This is **Step 7**: the smoke test, and it's a *big* one. We're going to hit the `consul_development` database, which, remember, is production-like and loaded with actual data – those 10 chains of related citizen-proposal rows are still in there, so we have a realistic test environment. The plan is to run this test in **READ-ONLY** mode! A full smoke test suite against a *real* production-like database.

My instinct is to use a transaction wrapped in `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.transaction { ...; raise ActiveRecord::Rollback }` to ensure any changes are rolled back. We're going to verify row counts before and after the test to confirm the data remains untouched. This is critical for preventing accidental modifications to the production-like data, which would invalidate the test's purpose.

This test is going to hit every major endpoint in the application. We're going to simulate real user behavior through `ActionDispatch::Integration::Session`, sending actual Rack requests via `Rails.application.call(...)`. We need to cover the spectrum of user roles: anonymous users, citizens (`amara`, `voter1`, `voter2`, `voter3`, `voter6`, `voter7`), moderators (`ines`), and the administrator (`admin`).

  conn = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
  before_counts = conn.tables.sort.to_h { |t| [t, conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM #{conn.quote_table_name(t)}").to_i] }

  conn.transaction do
    app = ActionDispatch::Integration::Session.new(Rails.application)
    app.host = "localhost"

    check_200 = lambda do |path|
      code = app.get(path)
      raise "Expected 200 on #{path}, got #{code}\n#{app.response.body[0, 500]}" unless code == 200
      puts "200 OK: #{path}"
    end

    check_404 = lambda do |path|
      begin
        code = app.get(path)
        raise "Expected 404 on #{path}, got #{code}" unless code == 404
      rescue ActionController::RoutingError, ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
        code = 404
      end
      puts "404 OK: #{path}"
    end

    # Anonymous requests
    %w[/ /debates /polls /budgets /legislation/processes /sdg/goals /sdg/goals/1 /help /users/2-amara /users/7-voter2 /users/12-voter7].each(&check_200)
    %w[/proposals /proposals/1 /proposal_notifications/1 /polls/which-bus-line-first /communities/2 /communities/2/topics/1 /comments/1 /comments/14].each(&check_404)

    end
    %w[/moderation/proposals /moderation/proposal_notifications].each do |p|

messages.content: Let's run the Deploy 1 -> Deploy 2 live process simulation with proper FK deletion order on `polls` to confirm Deploy 1 handles live table & column drops with zero errors!
messages.thinking:
Okay, let's break this down.

**Post-Simulation Victory and Follow-Up Actions**

That simulation was incredibly valuable! First, a critical win: every single `Legislation::Proposal` page, across various URL structures, returned a **200 OK** status. That's exactly what we needed to see, confirming the integrity of those endpoints after the recent changes.

Second, Deploy 2's simulation flagged a crucial foreign key (FK) deletion order issue with polls. It highlighted the dependency chain: `poll_question_answer_translations -> poll_question_answers -> poll_question_translations & votation_types -> poll_questions -> poll_translations -> polls`. The simulation served as a refresher and a preventative measure by highlighting the correct FK deletion order to prevent errors. We need to document the exact deletion order in `docs/REMOVAL.md` for Deploy 2. It will save a lot of headaches later.

To ensure confidence in the live processes following Deploy 2, I'm going to re-run the Deploy 2 simulation. This time, I'll delete `poll_questions` in the correct FK order. This will verify that our post-Deploy-2 live process check works as expected. We need to be thorough.

set -e && cd /app && bundle exec rails runner '
  conn = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
  before_counts = conn.tables.sort.to_h { |t| [t, conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM #{conn.quote_table_name(t)}").to_i] }

  conn.transaction do
    app = ActionDispatch::Integration::Session.new(Rails.application)
    app.host = "localhost"
    Warden.test_mode!
    admin = User.find(1)

    check_200 = lambda do |path|
      code = app.get(path)
      raise "Expected 200 on #{path}, got #{code}\n#{app.response.body[0, 500]}" unless code == 200
      puts "200 OK: #{path}"
    end

    # Prime prepared statements & schema caches BEFORE Deploy 2 migration!
    10.times do
      app.get("/")
      app.get("/debates")
      app.get("/polls")
      app.get("/users/2-amara")
      Warden.on_next_request { |proxy| proxy.set_user(admin, scope: :user) }
      app.get("/account")
      Warden.on_next_request { |proxy| proxy.set_user(admin, scope: :user) }
      app.get("/admin/stats")
      Warden.on_next_request { |proxy| proxy.set_user(admin, scope: :user) }
      app.get("/admin/polls")
      Warden.on_next_request { |proxy| proxy.set_user(admin, scope: :user) }
      app.get("/admin/tags")
    end

    # Simulate Deploy 2 migration!
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM dashboard_administrator_tasks")
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM dashboard_executed_actions")
    conn.execute("DROP TABLE dashboard_administrator_tasks, dashboard_executed_actions, dashboard_actions, links, proposal_notifications, proposal_translations")
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM votation_types WHERE questionable_type = '\''Poll::Question'\'' AND questionable_id IN (SELECT id FROM poll_questions WHERE poll_id IN (SELECT id FROM polls WHERE related_type = '\''Proposal'\''))")
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM poll_question_answer_translations WHERE poll_question_answer_id IN (SELECT id FROM poll_question_answers WHERE question_id IN (SELECT id FROM poll_questions WHERE poll_id IN (SELECT id FROM polls WHERE related_type = '\''Proposal'\'')))")
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM poll_question_answers WHERE question_id IN (SELECT id FROM poll_questions WHERE poll_id IN (SELECT id FROM polls WHERE related_type = '\''Proposal'\''))")
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM poll_question_translations WHERE poll_question_id IN (SELECT id FROM poll_questions WHERE poll_id IN (SELECT id FROM polls WHERE related_type = '\''Proposal'\''))")
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM poll_questions WHERE poll_id IN (SELECT id FROM polls WHERE related_type = '\''Proposal'\'')")
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM poll_translations WHERE poll_id IN (SELECT id FROM polls WHERE related_type = '\''Proposal'\'')")
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM polls WHERE related_type = '\''Proposal'\''")
    conn.execute("ALTER TABLE poll_questions DROP COLUMN proposal_id")
    conn.execute("ALTER TABLE polls DROP COLUMN related_type, DROP COLUMN related_id")
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM map_locations WHERE proposal_id IS NOT NULL AND investment_id IS NULL")
    conn.execute("ALTER TABLE map_locations DROP COLUMN proposal_id")
    conn.execute("ALTER TABLE tags DROP COLUMN proposals_count")
    conn.execute("ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN recommended_proposals, DROP COLUMN email_digest, DROP COLUMN failed_email_digests_count")
    conn.execute("DROP TABLE proposals")

    puts "--- TESTING ALREADY-WARMED DEPLOY 1 PROCESS AFTER DEPLOY 2 DROPS TABLES & COLUMNS ---"
    %w[/ /debates /polls /budgets /legislation/processes /sdg/goals /users/2-amara].each(&check_200)
    %w[/account /admin/stats /admin/polls /admin/tags /admin/banners/new /admin/homepage].each do |p|
      Warden.on_next_request { |proxy| proxy.set_user(admin, scope: :user) }
      check_200.call(p)
    end

    raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
  end

  after_counts = conn.tables.sort.to_h { |t| [t, conn.select_value("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM #{conn.quote_table_name(t)}").to_i] }
  raise "DB counts changed!" unless before_counts == after_counts
  puts "ZERO-DOWNTIME SIMULATION PASSED 100% AND DEV DB UNTOUCHED!"
'

messages.thinking:
**Alright, time to think this through and get this done flawlessly.** The zero-downtime simulation passed perfectly, and the development database remains untouched. That's a huge relief! The existing Rails process handled all those requests without a hitch even after a `DROP TABLE` and `ALTER TABLE` statement, which is excellent confirmation.

Okay, let's craft a really robust RSpec spec, probably a request spec, to guarantee the routing is exactly as required. We need to make sure all those old citizen-proposal routes are *gone*, and the legislation proposal routes *still* work. Crucially, we have to test that there are no leaks into existing queries with our transitional polymorphic safety measures.

Now, wait a second! We're using `i18n-tasks` here, right? We need to verify that our new spec isn't going to get the i18n scanner to look in the spec folder, and since it usually only scans the 'app/' directory we should be good. Also, RuboCop should be running on the `spec/` directory so we'll be able to confirm our spec is linting correctly.

Let's dive into that documentation file (`docs/REMOVAL.md`) and make sure we have *everything* documented. This is a multi-step operation, so clear, complete notes are absolutely critical for our future selves and this will have to pass `mdl`.

Here’s the current plan, in my own words:

*   **Deploy 1**: The current code removal phase will require changes, but no database migrations yet! Just code removal, `ignored_columns`, and transitional polymorphic `default_scope`s. The schema and development database are to remain untouched, to keep the current release running with zero downtime.
*   **Deploy 2**: This is where things get real. We dump *everything* we are getting rid of into files under `db/`, in a safe order so FK dependencies are respected, then run the database migrations: delete citizen-proposal-linked rows, drop foreign keys, drop citizen-proposal columns, and drop tables. This must be safe alongside Deploy 1 because Deploy 1 will have `ignored_columns` and no queries to those dropped tables.
*   **Deploy 3**: We'll clean up the code. Remove the `ignored_columns` from the models and the `default_scope`s and update the code where needed.

**Crucial Notes:** We need to back up everything *before* deleting it! The instructions specify storing these backups under `db/`. We must ensure the backups don’t get tracked by git, but rather reside on the development database. # Citizen Proposals Removal Plan & Progress

Citizen proposals (`Proposal`), author notifications (`ProposalNotification` and
`EmailDigest`), the proposal authors' dashboard (`Dashboard::Action`,
`Dashboard::ExecutedAction`, `Dashboard::AdministratorTask`, `Link`), and all
associated public, admin, moderation, management, SDG, and GraphQL screens are
being retired across **three zero-downtime deploys**.

Legislation proposals (`Legislation::Proposal`) are a separate feature and stay.

---

## Deploy 1 — Remove Application Code & Prepare Zero-Downtime Shims (Prepared)

Status: **Prepared in repository (ready to ship; no database migrations in Deploy 1).**

### Why no database changes in Deploy 1

While Deploy 1 rolls out, servers running the previous release continue serving
traffic against PostgreSQL (`consul_development`). Leaving all tables, columns,
foreign keys, and rows untouched ensures the previous release keeps running
without errors during the rollout.

### What changed in Deploy 1

1. **Removed citizen proposal models, concerns, and mailers/jobs**
   - Deleted `Proposal`, `Proposal::Exporter`, `ProposalNotification`,
     `Dashboard`, `Dashboard::Action`, `Dashboard::AdministratorTask`,
     `Dashboard::ExecutedAction`, `Link`, `Linkable`, `EmailDigest`, and
     `Dashboard::Mailer`.
   - Removed `Mailer#proposal_notification_digest` and
     `Notification.send_pending`.
   - Removed `all_proposal_authors` and `proposal_authors` from `UserSegments`.
   - Removed citizen proposal export/import/cleanup pipelines from
     `MachineLearning`.
   - Removed `proposal_created` from `Ahoy::Chart`.

2. **Removed routes, controllers, components, views, helpers, GraphQL types, and assets**
   - Deleted `config/routes/proposal.rb` and removed `draw :proposal` from
     `config/routes.rb`.
   - Removed citizen proposal, proposal notification, and proposal dashboard
     routes from `config/routes/{admin,moderation,management,notification}.rb`
     and `config/sitemap.rb`.
   - Deleted `ProposalsController`, `ProposalNotificationsController`,
     `DashboardController`, `Dashboard::*Controller`,
     `Admin::ProposalsController`, `Admin::ProposalMilestonesController`,
     `Admin::ProposalProgressBarsController`, `Admin::HiddenProposalsController`,
     `Admin::HiddenProposalNotificationsController`,
     `Admin::Dashboard::{Actions,AdministratorTasks,Base}Controller` (kept
     `Admin::DashboardController` for `/admin`),
     `Moderation::ProposalsController`,
     `Moderation::ProposalNotificationsController` (kept
     `Moderation::Legislation::ProposalsController` and
     `Moderation::DashboardController`), and `Management::ProposalsController`
     (kept `Management::DashboardController`).
   - Deleted citizen proposal, proposal dashboard, and proposal feed components,
     views, helpers, JS (`dashboard_graphs.js`,
     `admin/dashboard/actions/form.js`), SCSS, and images; kept
     `Admin::Proposals::ToggleSelectionComponent` and `proposals/new.scss` which
     are used by `Legislation::Proposal`, and fixed
     `Legislation::Proposals::VotesComponent` share URL to use
     `legislation_process_proposal_url`.
   - Deleted `Types::ProposalType` and `Types::ProposalNotificationType`, and
     removed `proposal`, `proposals`, `proposal_notification`,
     `proposal_notifications`, and `public_proposals` from GraphQL `QueryType`
     and `UserType`.
   - Updated `CanCan` abilities, navigation menus, settings tabs, stats, system
     emails, communities/topics, polls, welcome recommendations, account
     preferences, subscriptions, signature sheets, SDG relatables, dev seeds,
     welcome page templates, and English locale files (`config/locales/en/*.yml`
     and `config/i18n-tasks.yml`).
   - Kept `Setting` keys `max_votes_for_proposal_edit` and
     `proposal_code_prefix` because `Legislation::Proposal` uses both.

3. **Added zero-downtime `ignored_columns` on kept models (for Deploy 2)**
   - `User`: `recommended_proposals`, `email_digest`,
     `failed_email_digests_count`
   - `ActsAsTaggableOn::Tag` (`config/initializers/acts_as_taggable_on.rb`):
     `proposals_count`
   - `Poll`: `related_type`, `related_id`
   - `Poll::Question`: `proposal_id`
   - `MapLocation`: `proposal_id`

4. **Added transitional `default_scope` filters on kept polymorphic/shared models**
   - Prevents `NameError` or broken links while citizen proposal rows remain in
     the database during Deploy 1 and while Deploy 2 migrates:
     - `Activity` (`app/models/activity.rb`)
     - `Comment` (`app/models/comment.rb`)
     - `Document` (`app/models/document.rb`)
     - `Flag` (`app/models/flag.rb`)
     - `Follow` (`app/models/follow.rb`)
     - `Image` (`app/models/image.rb`)
     - `Milestone` (`app/models/milestone.rb`)
     - `MlSummaryComment` (`app/models/ml_summary_comment.rb`)
     - `Notification` (`app/models/notification.rb`)

       the query stays valid both before and after `related_type` is dropped in
       Deploy 2)
     - `ProgressBar` (`app/models/progress_bar.rb`)
     - `RelatedContent` (`app/models/related_content.rb`)

     - `WebSection` (`app/models/web_section.rb`)
     - `Widget::Feed` (`app/models/widget/feed.rb`)

---

## Deploy 2 — Archive Data & Remove Tables, Columns, and Dependent Rows (Remaining)

Once Deploy 1 has shipped and is the running release, prepare Deploy 2:

### 1. Dump all retiring data to `db/` before deleting or dropping anything

- Every table, column, and row removed from PostgreSQL must first be copied into
  tracked file(s) under `db/` (for example under `db/backups/` or
  `db/citizen_proposals_archive/`) and kept in the repository.
- **Important**: The development database (`consul_development`) is the one
  deploys migrate. Ensure running migrations in `RAILS_ENV=test` does not
  overwrite the non-empty dump captured from `consul_development`.

### 2. Clean up dependent and polymorphic rows in kept tables (after dumping)

Delete in foreign-key-safe order:

- **Proposal dashboard polls** (`polls WHERE related_type = 'Proposal'`) and all
  dependent poll records:
  - `poll_answers`, `poll_partial_results`, `poll_voters`, `poll_recounts`,
    `poll_officer_assignments`, `poll_shifts`, `poll_booth_assignments`,
    `poll_ballot_sheets`, `geozones_polls` for those `poll_id`s
  - `votation_types` (`questionable_type = 'Poll::Question'`) for questions of
    those polls
  - `poll_question_answer_videos`, `poll_question_answer_translations`,
    `poll_question_answers` (plus any `images`/`documents` on options) for
    questions of those polls
  - `poll_question_translations` and `poll_questions` for those polls
  - `comments`/`comment_translations`, `sdg_relations`, `sdg_reviews`, `images`,
    `reports` on those polls or their questions
  - `poll_translations` and `polls` (`WHERE related_type = 'Proposal'`)
- **Orphaned proposal communities & topics**:
  - `communities` belonging to `proposals.community_id` (not referenced by
    `budget_investments.community_id` or `legislation_proposals.community_id`),
    their `topics`, and comments (plus translations and 2nd-hop records) on
    those topics (note: remove or nullify `proposals.community_id` FK before
    deleting `communities`, or delete `communities` right after dropping
    `proposals` after capturing `proposals.community_id`!).
- **Comments on citizen proposals** (`comments WHERE commentable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  and their `comment_translations`, plus **second-hop records** referencing
  those comment IDs (and topic comment IDs):
  - `votes` (`votable_type = 'Comment'`)
  - `flags` (`flaggable_type = 'Comment'`)
  - `activities` (`actionable_type = 'Comment'`)
  - `notifications` (`notifiable_type = 'Comment'`)
- **Direct polymorphic and FK rows** referencing `'Proposal'`,
  `'ProposalNotification'`, `'Dashboard::Action'`, or
  `'Dashboard::ExecutedAction'`:
  - `votes` (`votable_type = 'Proposal'`) and `signatures`/`signature_sheets`
    (`signable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `follows` (`followable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `flags` (`flaggable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `activities` (`actionable_type IN ('Proposal', 'ProposalNotification')`)
  - `notifications` (`notifiable_type IN ('Proposal', 'ProposalNotification')`)
    and reset `users.notifications_count` to match remaining notifications
  - `related_content_scores` for proposal `related_contents`, then
    `related_contents` (`parent_relationable_type = 'Proposal' OR child_relationable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `taggings` (`taggable_type = 'Proposal'`) and recalculate
    `tags.taggings_count` (and remove orphan non-category tags if appropriate, or
    keep tags with `taggings_count = 0`)
  - `map_locations` (`WHERE proposal_id IS NOT NULL AND investment_id IS NULL`)
  - `documents` (`documentable_type IN ('Proposal', 'Dashboard::Action')`) and
    `images` (`imageable_type = 'Proposal'`) (and `active_storage_attachments`
    if any)
  - `milestone_translations`/`milestones` (`milestoneable_type = 'Proposal'`)
    and `progress_bar_translations`/`progress_bars` (`progressable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `sdg_relations` and `sdg_reviews` (`relatable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `ml_summary_comments` (`commentable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `remote_translations` (`remote_translatable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `audits` (`auditable_type = 'Proposal' OR associated_type = 'Proposal'`)
- **Configuration & CMS rows**:
  - `settings` rows for retired keys: `feature.featured_proposals`,
    `feature.user.recommendations_on_proposals`,
    `homepage.widgets.feeds.proposals`, `process.proposals`,
    `proposals.successful_proposal_id`, `proposals.poll_short_title`,
    `proposals.poll_description`, `proposals.poll_link`,
    `proposals.email_short_title`, `proposals.email_description`,
    `proposals.poster_short_title`, `proposals.poster_description`,
    `votes_for_proposal_success`, `months_to_archive_proposals`,
    `proposal_notification_minimum_interval_in_days`,
    `featured_proposals_number`, `feature.dashboard.notification_emails`,
    `sdg.process.proposals` (keep `max_votes_for_proposal_edit` and
    `proposal_code_prefix`!)
  - `widget_feeds` (`WHERE kind = 'proposals'`)
  - `banner_sections` for the `proposals` web section, then `web_sections`
    (`WHERE name = 'proposals'`)
  - `i18n_content_translations`/`i18n_contents` for retired `proposals.*` or
    `dashboard.*` keys (if any)

### 3. Drop citizen proposal columns on kept tables and drop citizen proposal tables

Because Deploy 1 already sets `ignored_columns` on all five kept models and
never queries the retiring tables, Deploy 2 can safely drop:

- Foreign keys & columns on kept tables:
  - `poll_questions.proposal_id` (and FK to `proposals`)
  - `polls.related_type`, `polls.related_id`
  - `map_locations.proposal_id`
  - `tags.proposals_count`
  - `users.recommended_proposals`, `users.email_digest`,
    `users.failed_email_digests_count`
- Tables (in FK-safe order):
  1. `dashboard_administrator_tasks`

  3. `dashboard_actions`
  4. `links`
  5. `proposal_notifications`
  6. `proposal_translations`
  7. `proposals`

---

Once Deploy 2 has shipped and migrated `consul_development`, prepare Deploy 3:

set -e && cd /app && cat <<'EOF' > docs/REMOVAL.md
# Citizen Proposals Removal Plan & Progress

Citizen proposals (`Proposal`), author notifications (`ProposalNotification` and
`EmailDigest`), the proposal authors' dashboard (`Dashboard::Action`,
`Dashboard::ExecutedAction`, `Dashboard::AdministratorTask`, `Link`), and all
associated public, admin, moderation, management, SDG, and GraphQL screens are
being retired across **three zero-downtime deploys**.

Legislation proposals (`Legislation::Proposal`) are a separate feature and stay.

---

## Deploy 1 — Remove Application Code & Prepare Zero-Downtime Shims (Prepared)

Status: **Prepared in repository (ready to ship; no database migrations in Deploy 1).**

### Why no database changes in Deploy 1

While Deploy 1 rolls out, servers running the previous release continue serving
traffic against PostgreSQL (`consul_development`). Leaving all tables, columns,
foreign keys, and rows untouched ensures the previous release keeps running
without errors during the rollout.

### What changed in Deploy 1

#### 1. Removed citizen proposal models, concerns, and mailers/jobs

- Deleted `Proposal`, `Proposal::Exporter`, `ProposalNotification`, `Dashboard`,
  `Dashboard::Action`, `Dashboard::AdministratorTask`,
  `Dashboard::ExecutedAction`, `Link`, `Linkable`, `EmailDigest`, and
  `Dashboard::Mailer`.
- Removed `Mailer#proposal_notification_digest` and `Notification.send_pending`.
- Removed `all_proposal_authors` and `proposal_authors` from `UserSegments`.
- Removed citizen proposal export/import/cleanup pipelines from
  `MachineLearning`.
- Removed `proposal_created` from `Ahoy::Chart`.

#### 2. Removed routes, controllers, components, views, helpers, GraphQL types, and assets

- Deleted `config/routes/proposal.rb` and removed `draw :proposal` from
  `config/routes.rb`.
- Removed citizen proposal, proposal notification, and proposal dashboard routes
  from `config/routes/{admin,moderation,management,notification}.rb` and
  `config/sitemap.rb`.
- Deleted `ProposalsController`, `ProposalNotificationsController`,
  `DashboardController`, `Dashboard::*Controller`, `Admin::ProposalsController`,
  `Admin::ProposalMilestonesController`,
  `Admin::ProposalProgressBarsController`, `Admin::HiddenProposalsController`,
  `Admin::HiddenProposalNotificationsController`,
  `Admin::Dashboard::{Actions,AdministratorTasks,Base}Controller` (kept
  `Admin::DashboardController` for `/admin`), `Moderation::ProposalsController`,
  `Moderation::ProposalNotificationsController` (kept
  `Moderation::Legislation::ProposalsController` and
  `Moderation::DashboardController`), and `Management::ProposalsController` (kept
  `Management::DashboardController`).
- Deleted citizen proposal, proposal dashboard, and proposal feed components,
  views, helpers, JS (`dashboard_graphs.js`,
  `admin/dashboard/actions/form.js`), SCSS, and images; kept
  `Admin::Proposals::ToggleSelectionComponent` and `proposals/new.scss` which
  are used by `Legislation::Proposal`, and fixed
  `Legislation::Proposals::VotesComponent` share URL to use
  `legislation_process_proposal_url`.
- Deleted `Types::ProposalType` and `Types::ProposalNotificationType`, and
  removed `proposal`, `proposals`, `proposal_notification`,
  `proposal_notifications`, and `public_proposals` from GraphQL `QueryType` and
  `UserType`.
- Updated `CanCan` abilities, navigation menus, settings tabs, stats, system
  emails, communities/topics, polls, welcome recommendations, account
  preferences, subscriptions, signature sheets, SDG relatables, dev seeds,
  welcome page templates, and English locale files (`config/locales/en/*.yml`
  and `config/i18n-tasks.yml`).
- Kept `Setting` keys `max_votes_for_proposal_edit` and `proposal_code_prefix`
  because `Legislation::Proposal` uses both.

#### 3. Added zero-downtime `ignored_columns` on kept models (for Deploy 2)

- `User`: `recommended_proposals`, `email_digest`, `failed_email_digests_count`
- `ActsAsTaggableOn::Tag` (`config/initializers/acts_as_taggable_on.rb`):
  `proposals_count`
- `Poll`: `related_type`, `related_id`
- `Poll::Question`: `proposal_id`
- `MapLocation`: `proposal_id`

#### 4. Added transitional `default_scope` filters on kept polymorphic/shared models

Prevents `NameError` or broken links while citizen proposal rows remain in the
database during Deploy 1 and while Deploy 2 migrates:

- `Activity` (`app/models/activity.rb`)
- `Comment` (`app/models/comment.rb`)
- `Document` (`app/models/document.rb`)
- `Flag` (`app/models/flag.rb`)
- `Follow` (`app/models/follow.rb`)
- `Image` (`app/models/image.rb`)
- `Milestone` (`app/models/milestone.rb`)
- `MlSummaryComment` (`app/models/ml_summary_comment.rb`)
- `Notification` (`app/models/notification.rb`)
- `Poll` (`app/models/poll.rb` — uses `to_jsonb(polls)->>'related_type'` so the
  query stays valid both before and after `related_type` is dropped in Deploy 2)
- `ProgressBar` (`app/models/progress_bar.rb`)
- `RelatedContent` (`app/models/related_content.rb`)
- `RemoteTranslation` (`app/models/remote_translation.rb`)
- `SDG::Relation` (`app/models/sdg/relation.rb`)
- `SignatureSheet` (`app/models/signature_sheet.rb`)
- `ActsAsTaggableOn::Tagging` (`config/initializers/acts_as_taggable_on.rb`)

- `ActsAsVotable::Vote` (`config/initializers/vote_extensions.rb`)
- `WebSection` (`app/models/web_section.rb`)
- `Widget::Feed` (`app/models/widget/feed.rb`)

---

## Deploy 2 — Archive Data & Remove Tables, Columns, and Dependent Rows (Remaining)

Once Deploy 1 has shipped and is the running release, prepare Deploy 2:

### 1. Dump all retiring data to `db/` before deleting or dropping anything

- Every table, column, and row removed from PostgreSQL must first be copied into
  tracked file(s) under `db/` (for example under `db/backups/` or
  `db/citizen_proposals_archive/`) and kept in the repository.
- **Important**: The development database (`consul_development`) is the one
  deploys migrate. Ensure running migrations in `RAILS_ENV=test` does not
  overwrite the non-empty dump captured from `consul_development`.

### 2. Clean up dependent and polymorphic rows in kept tables (after dumping)

Delete in foreign-key-safe order:

- **Proposal dashboard polls** (`polls WHERE related_type = 'Proposal'`) and all
  dependent poll records:
  - `poll_answers`, `poll_partial_results`, `poll_voters`, `poll_recounts`,
    `poll_officer_assignments`, `poll_shifts`, `poll_booth_assignments`,
    `poll_ballot_sheets`, `geozones_polls` for those `poll_id`s
  - `votation_types` (`questionable_type = 'Poll::Question'`) for questions of
    those polls
  - `poll_question_answer_videos`, `poll_question_answer_translations`,
    `poll_question_answers` (plus any `images`/`documents` on options) for
    questions of those polls
  - `poll_question_translations` and `poll_questions` for those polls
  - `comments`/`comment_translations`, `sdg_relations`, `sdg_reviews`, `images`,
    `reports` on those polls or their questions
  - `poll_translations` and `polls` (`WHERE related_type = 'Proposal'`)
- **Orphaned proposal communities & topics**:
  - `communities` belonging to `proposals.community_id` (not referenced by
    `budget_investments.community_id` or `legislation_proposals.community_id`),
    their `topics`, and comments (plus translations and 2nd-hop records) on
    those topics (remove or nullify `proposals.community_id` FK before deleting
    `communities`, or delete `communities` right after dropping `proposals`
    after capturing `proposals.community_id`).
- **Comments on citizen proposals** (`comments WHERE commentable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  and their `comment_translations`, plus **second-hop records** referencing
  those comment IDs (and topic comment IDs):
  - `votes` (`votable_type = 'Comment'`)
  - `flags` (`flaggable_type = 'Comment'`)
  - `activities` (`actionable_type = 'Comment'`)
  - `notifications` (`notifiable_type = 'Comment'`)
- **Direct polymorphic and FK rows** referencing `'Proposal'`,
  `'ProposalNotification'`, `'Dashboard::Action'`, or
  `'Dashboard::ExecutedAction'`:
  - `votes` (`votable_type = 'Proposal'`) and `signatures`/`signature_sheets`
    (`signable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `follows` (`followable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `flags` (`flaggable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `activities` (`actionable_type IN ('Proposal', 'ProposalNotification')`)
  - `notifications` (`notifiable_type IN ('Proposal', 'ProposalNotification')`)
    and reset `users.notifications_count` to match remaining notifications
  - `related_content_scores` for proposal `related_contents`, then
    `related_contents` (`parent_relationable_type = 'Proposal' OR child_relationable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `taggings` (`taggable_type = 'Proposal'`) and recalculate
    `tags.taggings_count`
  - `map_locations` (`WHERE proposal_id IS NOT NULL AND investment_id IS NULL`)
  - `documents` (`documentable_type IN ('Proposal', 'Dashboard::Action')`) and
    `images` (`imageable_type = 'Proposal'`) (and `active_storage_attachments`
    if any)
  - `milestone_translations`/`milestones` (`milestoneable_type = 'Proposal'`)
    and `progress_bar_translations`/`progress_bars` (`progressable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `sdg_relations` and `sdg_reviews` (`relatable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `ml_summary_comments` (`commentable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `remote_translations` (`remote_translatable_type = 'Proposal'`)
  - `audits` (`auditable_type = 'Proposal' OR associated_type = 'Proposal'`)
- **Configuration & CMS rows**:
  - `settings` rows for retired keys: `feature.featured_proposals`,
    `feature.user.recommendations_on_proposals`,
    `homepage.widgets.feeds.proposals`, `process.proposals`,
    `proposals.successful_proposal_id`, `proposals.poll_short_title`,
    `proposals.poll_description`, `proposals.poll_link`,
    `proposals.email_short_title`, `proposals.email_description`,
    `proposals.poster_short_title`, `proposals.poster_description`,
    `votes_for_proposal_success`, `months_to_archive_proposals`,
    `proposal_notification_minimum_interval_in_days`,
    `featured_proposals_number`, `feature.dashboard.notification_emails`,
    `sdg.process.proposals` (keep `max_votes_for_proposal_edit` and
    `proposal_code_prefix`)
  - `widget_feeds` (`WHERE kind = 'proposals'`)
  - `banner_sections` for the `proposals` web section, then `web_sections`
    (`WHERE name = 'proposals'`)
  - `i18n_content_translations`/`i18n_contents` for retired `proposals.*` or
    `dashboard.*` keys (if any)

### 3. Drop citizen proposal columns on kept tables and drop citizen proposal tables

Because Deploy 1 already sets `ignored_columns` on all five kept models and
never queries the retiring tables, Deploy 2 can safely drop:

- **Foreign keys & columns on kept tables**:
  - `poll_questions.proposal_id` (and FK to `proposals`)
  - `polls.related_type`, `polls.related_id`
  - `map_locations.proposal_id`
  - `tags.proposals_count`
  - `users.recommended_proposals`, `users.email_digest`,
    `users.failed_email_digests_count`
- **Tables** (in FK-safe order):
  - `dashboard_administrator_tasks`
  - `dashboard_executed_actions`
  - `dashboard_actions`
  - `links`
  - `proposal_notifications`
  - `proposal_translations`
  - `proposals`

I have prepared **Deploy 1** for retiring citizen proposals with zero downtime, and recorded full notes for all three deploys in `docs/REMOVAL.md`.

### Summary of Deploy 1

1. **Retired citizen proposal features in application code**
   - Removed citizen proposals (`Proposal`), author notifications (`ProposalNotification` and `EmailDigest`), and the proposal authors' dashboard (`Dashboard::Action`, `Dashboard::ExecutedAction`, `Dashboard::AdministratorTask`, and dashboard action `Link`s), along with their public, admin, moderation, management, SDG, sitemap, and GraphQL routes, controllers, views, components, helpers, mailers, and assets.
   - Kept collaborative legislation proposals (`Legislation::Proposal`) and all other participation modules (debates, polls, participatory budgets, SDG) intact.
   - Cleaned unused citizen-proposal English strings from `config/locales/en/` and `config/i18n-tasks.yml` (`spec/i18n_spec.rb` passes).

2. **Zero-downtime preparation (safe next to both the previous release and Deploy 2)**
   - **No database tables, columns, or rows were removed in Deploy 1** (`db/schema.rb` and `consul_development` are unchanged), so the currently running servers keep working while Deploy 1 rolls out.
   - Added `ignored_columns` on kept models (`User`, `Tag`, `Poll`, `Poll::Question`, `MapLocation`) so Deploy 1 servers will keep running safely when Deploy 2 drops those columns.
   - Added transitional scopes on kept polymorphic/shared models (`Comment`, `Vote`, `Follow`, `Flag`, `Notification`, `Activity`, `Poll`, `Topic`, `RelatedContent`, etc.) so existing database records pointing at citizen proposals do not cause errors while Deploy 1 serves traffic.

3. **Roadmap in `docs/REMOVAL.md`**
   - **Deploy 2 (next):** Dump all citizen-proposal tables, columns, and linked rows to `db/`, then remove those rows, columns, foreign keys, and tables.
   - **Deploy 3 (final):** Remove the temporary `ignored_columns` declarations and transitional scopes once the database cleanup has shipped.
